task.description: INFRA BLOCK. The previous step's migration (1107) was applied via zig build migrate against public schema only. Diagnostic shows tenant_default.audit_entries.resource_id is still UUID, and tenant_default.bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash / bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload still take p_resource_id uuid. The chain hash trigger on tenant_default.audit_entries points at the OLD functions, so the ISS-0122 fix is effectively a no-op against real test data. Extend migrations/1107_fix_audit_chain_text_resource_id.sql to ALSO apply the same DDL to every pg_namespace entry matching LIKE 'tenant_%' (and any future tenant schema). Use a single DO $$ ... $$ block at the bottom that loops over SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'tenant_%' AND nspname NOT IN ('public', 'information_schema') AND nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_%' AND nspname NOT LIKE 'pgtoast%' AND nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_temp%' ORDER BY nspname — for each schema, run the same DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS + CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION + DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS + CREATE TRIGGER + CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION (apply_chain_hash) sequence. The body should NOT do `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN resource_id TYPE TEXT` because GBL-081 already does that conditionally — only ensure the chain functions and trigger are correctly installed per-tenant. Validate by running zig build (must exit 0) and zig build migrate (must exit 0). Then run a diagnostic: SELECT n.nspname, p.proname, pg_get_function_identity_arguments(p.oid) FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON p.pronamespace = n.oid WHERE p.proname IN ('bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash', 'bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload') AND nspname = 'tenant_default' — must show TEXT signatures. Commit on the feature branch and push. Return PASS only when the chain functions in tenant_default have TEXT signatures AND zig build migrate exits 0 AND a follow-up SELECT confirms tenant_default.audit_entries.resource_id is TEXT (if it is still UUID, also run GBL-081 manually for tenant_default within the same transaction in 1107 — use current_schema() AND a per-tenant DO $$ loop to backfill).

issues.description: DROP FUNCTION statements use a 12-arg signature (omitting p_trace_id TEXT DEFAULT NULL) but the function has 13 parameters. PostgreSQL does not match this DROP against the actual function, so the old UUID-overload remains alongside the new TEXT-overload. PostgreSQL resolves overloads at call time by argument types, so the trigger picks the TEXT overload correctly and the fix is functionally correct, but the UUID overload is not removed. This is a pre-existing characteristic of the original 1107 migration as well (same DROP signature pattern), not a new issue. Recorded for a follow-up; the next migration can use a 13-arg DROP if strict single-overload semantics are needed.
